terms.gloss: a low eating house, of ill repute as the haunt of prostitutes
evidence: Cic. Pis. 13: in illō gāneārum tuārum nīdōre atque fūmō (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: the same word in its older form
evidence: Plaut. Men. 703: immersit aliquō sēsē, crēdō, in gāneum
Ter. Ad. 359: crēdō abductum in gāneum

terms.gloss: dens of vice, brothels; and the life led in them
evidence: Plaut. Cas. 242c: Ubi in lustra jacuistī?
Cic. Phil. 13.24: in lustrīs, popīnīs, āleā, vīnō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly the wallows and lairs of wild beasts (Festus, in Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: paulisper stetimus in illō gāneārum tuārum nīdōre atque fūmō
phrases.english: we stood for a little while in the reek and smoke of those dives of yours

phrases.latin: immersit aliquō sēsē, crēdō, in gāneum
phrases.english: he’s plunged into some dive or other, I suppose

phrases.latin: Ubi in lustra jacuistī? — Egone in lustra?
phrases.english: Which den of vice have you been lying in? — Me, in a den of vice?

sources: Lewis & Short: ganea · Lewis & Short: lustrum
